question: What do we call the study of human tissues?
explanation: Histology is simply the study of tissues under the microscope. Think of it as zooming in to see how cells team up!

question: Why do cells in a tissue live surrounded by an extracellular matrix?

options.A: To hold the cells together and help them share a common function
options.B: To generate electrical impulses for the nervous system automatically
options.C: To prevent any fluid from ever moving between the cells
options.D: To completely isolate each cell from its neighbors for protection

explanation: The extracellular matrix acts like mortar in a brick wall, holding the cells together so they can work as a solid team.

question: Which body tissue is mainly responsible for movement and pumping blood?
explanation: Muscle tissue is built to contract and shorten, making it the powerhouse behind every movement you make.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four main tissue types in the human body?
explanation: Adipose (fat) tissue is actually a type of connective tissue, not one of the four big primary tissue categories.

question: What is an epithelial tissue made of just a single layer of cells called?
explanation: The word 'simple' here just means 'one layer thick'! This makes it great for letting things pass through easily.

question: Oxygen needs to move quickly across the tiny air sacs in the lungs. Which type of tissue lines these healthy air sacs?
explanation: Simple squamous cells are super thin and flat, making them the perfect 'shortcut' for gases like oxygen to slip across.

question: What is a major feature that sets connective tissue apart from epithelial tissue?

options.A: Its cells are always tightly packed together without space
options.B: It never has any blood supply running through it
options.C: It contains a large amount of extracellular matrix
options.D: It is found exclusively on the outer surface of the skin

explanation: Unlike epithelial cells which pack tightly together, connective tissue cells are spread out in a rich matrix of fibers and ground substance.

question: Why do injuries to tendons and ligaments take such a long time to heal?

options.A: They lack any nervous tissue to signal the brain about pain
options.B: They are constantly exposed to strong digestive enzymes
options.C: They have a relatively poor blood supply compared to other tissues
options.D: They are made entirely of dead cells that cannot replicate

explanation: Blood brings the healing nutrients! Because tendons and ligaments get less blood flow, repairs happen much more slowly.

question: Which muscle type is attached to your skeleton and under your conscious control?
explanation: Skeletal muscles are the ones you choose to move when you walk, dance, or lift objects.

question: What is the main job of glial cells in the nervous system?

options.A: To connect bone to bone across movable joints
options.B: To generate electrical impulses for muscle contraction
options.C: To support, protect, and nourish the neurons
options.D: To form a tough protective membrane around the brain

explanation: Think of glial cells as the supportive backup team—they take care of the neurons so the neurons can focus on sending signals!

question: Which body membrane lines closed internal cavities that do NOT open to the outside?
explanation: Serous membranes line closed cavities like your chest and abdomen, making a slippery fluid to cut down friction.

question: A patient has a stiff, painful knee joint. Which membrane inside the joint is likely failing to produce enough lubricating fluid?
explanation: Synovial membranes line our movable joints and pump out synovial fluid to keep movements smooth and pain-free.

question: Why is good nutrition and protein especially vital for patients healing from deep wounds like pressure sores?

options.A: Cells need building blocks to repair the extracellular matrix and regenerate tissue
options.B: Nutrition stops nervous tissue from sending pain signals to the brain
options.C: Vitamins automatically clean bacteria out of closed body cavities
options.D: Proteins completely replace the need for blood circulation in wounds

explanation: Your body can't rebuild damaged tissue out of nothing! Good protein gives cells the raw materials they need to patch things up.

question: After a severe heart attack, why is the long-term recovery of heart muscle function often limited?

options.A: Cardiac cells divide much faster than epithelial cells, causing chaotic overgrowth
options.B: The cutaneous membrane prevents blood from reaching the damaged chest muscle
options.C: Cardiac muscle tissue has very limited ability to regenerate and is often replaced by scar tissue
options.D: Smooth muscle completely takes over and alters the heart rate permanently

explanation: Heart muscle cells don't easily multiply to fix themselves. Instead, the body patches the area with scar tissue, which doesn't contract.
